passages.title: PWD ID application (QCitizen PWD ID) (online)
passages.text: PWD ID application (QCitizen PWD ID). Also called: PWD ID, PWD card, disability ID, apply for PWD ID, PWD ID, ID ng PWD, magparehistro bilang PWD. Channel: online. Office: QC E-Services portal. Link: https://qceservices.quezoncity.gov.ph/. Fee: Free (no fee). Processing time: 3 days. Requirements: QC E-Services account; Whole-body photo showing the disability [only if the answer to "What kind of disability do you have?" is apparent]; Certificate of Disability (from a specialist doctor) [only if the answer to "What kind of disability do you have?" is non_apparent; not needed if the answer to "Do you already have the certificate from your specialist?" is yes]; Medical certificate (cancer / rare disease) [only if the answer to "What kind of disability do you have?" is cancer_rare; not needed if the answer to "Do you already have the certificate from your specialist?" is yes]; Proof of residence: Barangay certificate / clearance (one of: Government-issued ID / Barangay certificate / clearance) [not needed if the answer to "Do you have a government-issued ID with your Quezon City address?" is yes]; 2x2 ID photo (and signature). Notes on requirements: Certificate of Disability (from a specialist doctor): Must be signed by the specialist for your disability type, not a family doctor or general physician. Steps: 1. Log in and choose the QCitizen ID eApplication icon 2. Complete personal information and tick “Yes” for the Persons With Disability sector 3. Upload requirements; a virtual ID shows on submission, then agree and submit 4. Monitor application status in your E-Services account Note: Non-apparent disability validation takes 2–3 days. Renewal of a white PWD ID is processed as a new application.

passages.title: PWD ID application (QCitizen PWD ID) (in person)
passages.text: PWD ID application (QCitizen PWD ID). Also called: PWD ID, PWD card, disability ID, apply for PWD ID, PWD ID, ID ng PWD, magparehistro bilang PWD. Channel: in person (walk-in). Office: Persons with Disability Affairs Office (PDAO), Ground Floor, Community Center Building, Gate 3, Kalayaan Ave., QC Hall Compound, phone 8988-4242 loc 7809. Fee: Free (no fee). Processing time: 40 minutes. Requirements: Whole-body photo showing the disability [only if the answer to "What kind of disability do you have?" is apparent]; Certificate of Disability (from a specialist doctor) [only if the answer to "What kind of disability do you have?" is non_apparent; not needed if the answer to "Do you already have the certificate from your specialist?" is yes]; Medical certificate (cancer / rare disease) [only if the answer to "What kind of disability do you have?" is cancer_rare; not needed if the answer to "Do you already have the certificate from your specialist?" is yes]; Proof of residence: Barangay certificate / clearance (one of: Government-issued ID / Barangay certificate / clearance) [not needed if the answer to "Do you have a government-issued ID with your Quezon City address?" is yes]; 2x2 ID photo (and signature). Notes on requirements: Certificate of Disability (from a specialist doctor): Must be signed by the specialist for your disability type, not a family doctor or general physician. Steps: 1. Bring copies of requirements to PDAO for evaluation 2. Staff encode your information; it is approved and verified 3. Printed ID is given to you 4. Applicants with missing requirements are assisted and advised

passages.title: Certified True Copy of Birth Certificate (QC-registered) (in person)
passages.text: Certified True Copy of Birth Certificate (QC-registered). Also called: birth certificate copy, certified true copy of birth certificate, get birth certificate, kopya ng birth certificate. Channel: in person (walk-in). Office: City Civil Registry Department (CCRD), Quezon City Hall Compound (1st Floor, Door 2, Civic Center), phone 8988-4242 local 1516 (Birth Registration Division). Fee: PHP 65.00 per copy. Processing time: 15 minutes if on database (1945–2015); 3 days if manual search. Requirements: Request form for birth certificate (Information Desk); Government-issued / valid ID; Authorization letter/SPA + photocopies of owner’s and representative’s IDs [only if the answer to "Will a representative (someone other than the applicant) file this for you?" is yes]. Steps: 1. Submit filled-out request form and ID; receive order of payment 2. Pay at the City Treasurer’s cashier; receive claim stub 3. Receive the certified copy (Counter 5) Note: For persons born in Quezon City; counters 1 & 2.

passages.title: Certified True Copy of Birth Certificate (QC-registered) (online)
passages.text: Certified True Copy of Birth Certificate (QC-registered). Also called: birth certificate copy, certified true copy of birth certificate, get birth certificate, kopya ng birth certificate. Channel: online. Office: QC E-Services portal. Link: https://qceservices.quezoncity.gov.ph/. Fee: PHP 65.00 per copy. Processing time: 1–3 days plus 5 minutes at pick-up. Requirements: QC E-Services account; Authorization letter/SPA + photocopies of owner’s and representative’s IDs [only if the answer to "Will a representative (someone other than the applicant) file this for you?" is yes]. Steps: 1. Log in, click “Civil Registry Online Services”, then “Request for a Certificate” 2. Wait for the email saying the copy is ready for pick-up 3. Pick up at CCRD and pay at the City Treasurer’s Office

passages.title: Registration of Certificate of Live Birth (within 30 days) (in person)
passages.text: Registration of Certificate of Live Birth (within 30 days). Also called: register a birth, register newborn, certificate of live birth, iparehistro ang bagong silang na sanggol. Channel: in person (walk-in). Office: City Civil Registry Department (CCRD), Quezon City Hall Compound (1st Floor, Door 2, Civic Center), phone 8988-4242 local 1516 (Birth Registration Division). Fee: Free (no fee). Processing time: 5 minutes. Requirements: Duly accomplished Certificate of Live Birth (4 copies); Marriage Certificate of parents (PSA or local copy) [only if the answer to "Were the child’s parents married at the time of birth?" is yes]; Copy of valid IDs of parents; Notarized Affidavit of Admission of Paternity and/or Affidavit to Use the Surname of the Father [only if the answer to "Were the child’s parents married at the time of birth?" is no]. Notes on requirements: Duly accomplished Certificate of Live Birth (4 copies): From the hospital, maternity/lying-in clinic or birthing facility. Steps: 1. Submit the Certificate of Live Birth and all requirements at Counter 18 2. Receive the personal copy of the registered certificate

Requirements: QC E-Services account; Duly accomplished Certificate of Live Birth (4 copies); Marriage Certificate of parents (PSA or local copy) [only if the answer to "Were the child’s parents married at the time of birth?" is yes]; Copy of valid IDs of parents; Notarized Affidavit of Admission of Paternity and/or Affidavit to Use the Surname of the Father [only if the answer to "Were the child’s parents married at the time of birth?" is no]. passages.title: Pay business tax (City Treasurer’s Office) (in person)
passages.text: Pay business tax (City Treasurer’s Office). Also called: . Channel: in person (walk-in). Office: City Treasurer’s Office (CTO), Annex Building, Mayaman St. Brgy. Central, QC Hall Compound, Diliman, Quezon City, phone 8988-4242 locals 8317, 8145, 8156, 8157. Fee: As stated in the Business Tax Bill. Processing time: 10 minutes. Requirements: Computerized Business Tax Bill. Steps: 1. Present the approved Computerized Business Tax Bill at the payment counter 2. Pay; receive the computerized business tax official receipt Note: Online payment is also offered via QC E-Services (per the BPLD charter); details not captured here.

passages.title: Business permit renewal (online)
passages.text: Business permit renewal. Also called: renew business permit, mayor’s permit renewal, business permit, i-renew ang business permit, permit ng negosyo. Channel: online. Office: QC E-Services portal. Link: https://qceservices.quezoncity.gov.ph/. Fee: Free (no fee). Processing time: Not listed in the sources. Requirements: Previous Mayor’s Permit; Official Receipt of business tax payment (current year); Valid ID of business owner; Authorization form + valid ID of representative [only if the answer to "Will a representative (someone other than the applicant) file this for you?" is yes]. Steps: 1. Pay business tax 2. File renewal via QC E-Services portal or kiosks: Business One-Stop Shop → Apply for Mayor’s Permit (Business) → Renewal 3. Input Mayor’s Permit number and current-year business tax OR; submit requirements 4. Claim the renewed permit or have it delivered Note: Charter lists 30 minutes per evaluation stage but no single total; the system can auto-renew if compliant.

Requirements: QC E-Services account; Proof of birth date and address: Birth certificate + Barangay Certificate of Residency (one of: Valid ID showing birth date and address / Birth certificate + Barangay Certificate of Residency) [not needed if the answer to "Do you already have a QCitizen ID?" is yes]; Marriage Certificate [only if the answer to "Are you a married woman whose surname differs from your valid ID?" is yes]; 2x2 ID photo (and signature). passages.title: Building / construction permit (new construction) (online)
passages.text: Building / construction permit (new construction). Also called: building permit, construction permit, build a house, building permit, permit para magpatayo ng bahay. Channel: online. Office: Department of the Building Official (DBO), Ground to 3rd Floors, Civic Center D (BRO Bldg.), Mayaman Street, Quezon City Hall Compound, phone 8988-4242 Local 8902, 8903, 8905, 8909, 8916, 1400, 1401. Link: https://qceservices.quezoncity.gov.ph/. Fee: Refer to the Schedule of Fees (computed by DBO). Processing time: by class: 3 / 7 / 20 working days (simple: 3 working days, complex: 7 working days, highly_technical: 20 working days). Requirements: QC E-Services account; Registered private design/building professional (with QC E-Services account); Certified True Copy of Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) [only if the answer to "Are you the registered owner of the lot (named on the TCT)?" is yes]; Legal document showing right to build (e.g., Deed of Absolute Sale) when applicant is not the registered owner [only if the answer to "Are you the registered owner of the lot (named on the TCT)?" is no]; Notarized affidavits (forms printable from your QC E-Services account); Building plans with wet signature and seal of the design professional; Previous building permit / certificate of occupancy and approved plans (renovation; permit issued before Nov 17, 2022) [only if the answer to "Is this a renovation of a building whose permit was issued before Nov 17, 2022?" is yes]. Steps: 1. Log in to QC E-Services → Building Permit One-Stop Shop; generate application forms and checklist 2. Add or select building professionals; print checklist and forms 3. Electronically submit for pre-evaluation and schedule an appointment 4. Drop off documents at the DBO kiosk on your appointment date 5. Claim the Order of Payment (bring valid ID) and pay at the City Treasurer’s cashier 6. Return the OR; permit released Note: Payment window differs between sources: charter says Treasurer windows 13 or 14; the QCitizen guide says Counter 12. Confirm with DBO.

passages.title: PWD ID (PDAO) (in person)
passages.text: PWD ID (PDAO). Also called: PWD ID, PWD card, disability ID, apply for PWD ID, PWD ID, ID ng PWD, magparehistro bilang PWD. Channel: in person (walk-in). Office: Persons with Disability Affairs Office (PDAO), under CSWDO. Fee: Free (no fee). Processing time: 16 minutes. Requirements: Government-issued valid ID [not needed if the answer to "Do you have a valid government-issued ID?" is yes]; Medical certificate or Certificate of Non-Apparent Disability from the doctor [not needed if the answer to "Do you already have the medical certificate (or certificate of non-apparent disability) from your doctor?" is yes]; 1x1 ID picture; Whole-body picture. Notes on requirements: Medical certificate or Certificate of Non-Apparent Disability from the doctor: From a medical doctor, ophthalmologist, neurologist or orthopedic doctor. Steps: 1. Fill in the PWD form and be interviewed by the PDAO focal person 2. Submit requirements, including pictures; staff review them and record them in the log book 3. PWD card is issued and your information is encoded in the database 4. Optional: request other assistance (burial, medical, assistive device, if available) Note: Walk-in only in the sources read. The 2022 omnibus charter gives a different total (11 minutes and 10 seconds); the 2024 charter is used.

passages.title: Senior Citizen’s ID with booklet (OSCA) (in person)
passages.text: Senior Citizen’s ID with booklet (OSCA). Also called: senior citizen ID, OSCA ID, senior ID, senior card, ID ng senior, senior citizen card, OSCA ID. Channel: in person (walk-in). Office: Office for Senior Citizens Affairs (OSCA), Marikina City Hall, Shoe Avenue, Sta. Elena, Marikina City 1800 (floor/room inside the compound is not stated in the sources; confirm with the office), phone 8659-1956. Fee: Free (no fee). Processing time: 6 minutes. Requirements: Fully accomplished OSCA application form; 3 pcs. latest 1x1 ID picture; One valid ID or document (e.g., PhilSys National ID, UMID, voter’s ID, PRC ID, driver’s license, passport, birth certificate, barangay clearance) [not needed if the answer to "Do you have a valid ID or one of the accepted documents (e.g., birth certificate, barangay clearance)?" is yes]; Authorization letter signed by the senior citizen + valid ID of the senior citizen and of the representative [only if the answer to "Will a representative (someone other than the applicant) file this for you?" is yes]. Notes on requirements: Fully accomplished OSCA application form: Obtained from OSCA. Steps: 1. Submit the accomplished form with complete requirements; OSCA staff check them, interview you and encode your data 2. Claim the Senior Citizen’s ID and booklet Note: For Marikina residents aged 60 or older. Walk-in only in the sources read.

passages.title: Certified True Copy of Birth Certificate (Marikina-registered) (in person)
passages.text: Certified True Copy of Birth Certificate (Marikina-registered). Also called: birth certificate copy, certified true copy of birth certificate, get birth certificate, kopya ng birth certificate. Channel: in person (walk-in). Office: City Civil Registry Office (LCRO), Marikina City Hall, Shoe Avenue, Sta. Elena, Marikina City 1800 (floor/room inside the compound is not stated in the sources; confirm with the office), phone 8646-0373. Fee: PHP 150.00 per copy. Processing time: 6 minutes. Requirements: Request form for birth certificate (LCRO Window 4); Government-issued / valid ID of requester; Authorization letter / Special Power of Attorney from the document owner [only if the answer to "Will a representative (someone other than the applicant) file this for you?" is yes]. Steps: 1. Fill out the request form at LCRO Window 4 and submit it; the verifier checks availability in the database and issues the order of payment 2. Pay the CTC fee at the City Treasurer’s office and get the Official Receipt 3. Bring the OR to LCRO Window 4 to receive the certified copy Note: Records registered at the Marikina City Civil Registry only. The same fee is shown for birth, marriage and death copies. Walk-in only in the sources read.

passages.title: Registration of Certificate of Live Birth (on-time, within 30 days) (in person)
passages.text: Registration of Certificate of Live Birth (on-time, within 30 days). Also called: register a birth, register newborn, certificate of live birth, iparehistro ang bagong silang na sanggol. Channel: in person (walk-in). Office: City Civil Registry Office (LCRO), Marikina City Hall, Shoe Avenue, Sta. Elena, Marikina City 1800 (floor/room inside the compound is not stated in the sources; confirm with the office), phone 8646-0373. Fee: PHP 100.00 (on-time registration fee). Processing time: 9 minutes. Requirements: Properly accomplished Municipal Form 102 (Certificate of Live Birth), 1 set; Certified true copy or PSA/NSO copy of the parents’ marriage certificate [only if the answer to "Were the child’s parents married at the time of birth?" is yes]; Affidavit of Admission of Paternity (back of Form 102, signed by the parents and notarized) [only if the answer to "Were the child’s parents married at the time of birth?" is no]; Affidavit to Use the Surname of the Father (4 copies, signed by the mother and notarized) [only if the answer to "Were the child’s parents married at the time of birth?" is no]. Notes on requirements: Properly accomplished Municipal Form 102 (Certificate of Live Birth), 1 set: From the hospital, lying-in clinic or other birthing facility. Steps: 1. Submit the Certificate of Live Birth and requirements at LCRO; staff check completeness and give an order of payment 2. Pay the registration fee at the City Treasurer’s office 3. Bring the Official Receipt to LCRO Window 5 and get a claim stub with the release date Note: For births in Marikina City. Walk-in only in the sources read.

passages.title: Business permit renewal (BPLO) (online)
passages.text: Business permit renewal (BPLO). Also called: renew business permit, mayor’s permit renewal, business permit, i-renew ang business permit, permit ng negosyo. Channel: online. Office: Marikina Online Services portal. Link: https://payment.marikina.gov.ph/Marikina/OnlineServices/. Fee: Per the Revenue Code of Marikina City (computed by the portal). Processing time: 15 minutes (register and pay online). Requirements: Marikina Online Services account (payment.marikina.gov.ph); Business Account Number (from your existing Marikina business permit); Financial Statement / Quarterly VAT Returns / Monthly Percentage Tax (photocopies). Steps: 1. Sign in at payment.marikina.gov.ph, select Business Permit & Licensing Office, enter your Business Account Number and click Renew 2. Input the actual/annual declared gross sales and attach your financial statement and quarterly VAT, then Submit 3. Select the business and quarter to pay, Compute Business Tax, Proceed to Checkout and pay (credit/debit card, GCash, Maya or Bayad App) 4. An email confirmation is sent after a successful payment Note: Check your eBOSS compliance status first at https://bplo.marikina.gov.ph/client.

passages.title: Business permit renewal (BPLO) (in person)
passages.text: Business permit renewal (BPLO). Also called: renew business permit, mayor’s permit renewal, business permit, i-renew ang business permit, permit ng negosyo. Channel: in person (walk-in). Office: Business Permits and Licensing Office (BPLO), Ground Floor, Finance Bldg, Shoe Ave., Sta. Elena, Marikina City, phone 8244-1800 / 8646-2354. Fee: Per the Revenue Code of Marikina City (assessed by BPLO). Processing time: File 15 minutes, then pay 15 minutes. Requirements: eBOSS compliance (Engineering, BFP, CHO, CEMO); Financial Statement / Quarterly VAT Returns / Monthly Percentage Tax (photocopies); If through a representative: Authorization Letter/SPA (sole proprietorship) or Secretary’s Certificate (corporation, partnership, cooperative), plus valid IDs [only if the answer to "Will a representative (someone other than the applicant) file this for you?" is yes]; Public liability insurance. Notes on requirements: eBOSS compliance (Engineering, BFP, CHO, CEMO): Check your compliance status on the E-BOSS portal: https://bplo.marikina.gov.ph/client Public liability insurance: From any accredited insurance company (City Ordinance No. 32, Series of 2013). Steps: 1. File the duly accomplished application form with complete requirements at BPLO (evaluation, assessment, billing and permit) 2. Pay at the Treasury Office cashier 3. Payment due dates for the current year: Jan 20, Apr 20, Jul 20, Oct 20 (1st to 4th quarter) Note: The charter lists 15 minutes per stage (file, pay) with no single total.

passages.title: Building permit and other ancillary permits (OBO) (in person)
passages.text: Building permit and other ancillary permits (OBO). Also called: building permit, construction permit, build a house, building permit, permit para magpatayo ng bahay. Channel: in person (walk-in). Office: Office of the Building Official (OBO). Fee: Based on the Philippine Electrical Code, Mechanical Code and National Building Code. Processing time: 1 day and 3 hours. Requirements: TCT, Tax Declaration, Tax Receipt; Bill of materials and specifications; CSHP Certificate from DOLE; Locational Clearance; Signed and sealed construction plans (Architectural, Structural, Lot Plan, Electrical, Sanitary, Mechanical); Other government agency clearances, as required. Steps: 1. Submit complete requirements at the receiving section; the clerk checks the application 2. Two copies of the plan are endorsed to BFP 3. Technical evaluators check the electrical, sanitary, structural and architectural plans and property documents 4. The proposed construction is inspected 5. If compliant, the order of payment is prepared and approved; pay the permit fees at the cashier 6. The Building Official approves and the releasing clerk releases the permit Note: Classified Highly Technical in the 2024 charter. Walk-in only in the sources read.

Republic Act 9858 (legitimation of Children Born to Minor Parents) “This Law amended Article 177 of the Family Code which states that “Children conceived and born outside wedlock of parents who, at the time of the conception of the former, were not disqualified by any impediment to marry each other, or so disqualified only because either or both of them were below eighteen (18) years of age, may be legitimated.” Affidavit of Legitimation “Legitimation is a process where a child out of wedlock is considered legitimate by fiction of law due to the subsequent valid marriage of his/her parents. Affidavit of Legitimation is a joint statement of the parents of the illegitimate child where they declare the fact of their not being disqualified to marry each other at the time when the child was conceived at the fact, they subsequently married each other after the child was born.” II. passages.text: OFFICE OF THE BUILDING OFFICIAL CITIZEN’S CHARTER 2024 MANDATE : The Office of the City Building Official (OCBO), in consonance with the National Building Code of the Philippines, PD 1096 implements regulations and requirements for the construction, alteration, repair, conversion use, occupancy and demolition of buildings pursuant to Section 301 of PD 1096, as well as enforcement of related laws and ordinances, decisions and orders. MISSION : To provide and manage quality service, fast and efficient processing / evaluation of building and other ancillary permits and ensuring the safety of all infrastructure facilities as well as the best use, occupancy and maintenance of buildings and other structures. VISION : To effectively enforce strict compliance of all mandate under the National Building Code, PD 1096 and its implementing rules and regulations through the desired performance and work ethics of engineers and personnel under the Office of the City Building Official (OCBO). 123

URL: https://quezoncity.gov.ph/qcitizen-guides/how-to-apply-for-a-building-permit/ (Last updated on October 2, 2025) Log in to QC E-Services to generate the following: Building Permit Application forms Checklist of Requirements Click ‘Building Permit One-Stop Shop’. Electronically submit the documents for pre-evaluation. Schedule an appointment to physically submit the documentary requirements based on the checklist. Physically submit or drop-off the documentary requirements on the date of your appointment via the kiosk machine located at the Ground Floor of the Department of the Building Official, Civic Center D, Quezon City Hall Compound. Present a valid ID to claim the official assessment and fees or the ‘Order of Payment’. Pay the required fee at the Counter 12 of the City Treasurer’s Office, located at the Ground Floor of the Department of the Building Official.

passages.title: QCitizen Guide – How to Renew Business Permit, p. 1
passages.text: # Transcribed by Claude from browser read, 2026-11-18. URL: https://quezoncity.gov.ph/qcitizen-guides/how-to-renew-business-permit/ (Last updated on January 6, 2026) Filing a renewal application is required one (1) year from the issuance date of your permit. REQUIREMENTS: Official Receipt (machine validated) issued on the current year, from the City Treasurer’s Office Barangay Business Clearance (if already secured) Previous Business Permit Authorization Form (for application that will be processed by an authorized representative ONLINE APPLICATION: Pay your business tax. via the QC E-Services portal via the QC E-Services Kiosks located at the Quezon CIty Hall Compound Select ‘Renewal’. Input Mayor’s Permit Number and Business Tax Official Receipt of the current year. Wait for notification via email to claim the renewed permit in-person, or have it delivered via a courier of choice. Note: The online system is capable of auto-renewing a business permit if the establishment is compliant with all local regulatory requirements at the time of renewal.
